title: Ephesians COMA Study
description: 6-week walkthrough of Ephesians using the COMA method (Context, Observation, Meaning, Application) from a Reformed Baptist perspective

subsections.title: Introduction to Ephesians
subsections.content:
Paul wrote this letter from prison (likely Rome, around AD 60-62) to the church at Ephesus—a city known for its temple to Artemis and its practice of magic arts. Paul had spent nearly three years in Ephesus on his third missionary journey, making it one of the longest stays in any city during his ministry.

Ephesians is often called the 'Alps of the New Testament' because of its towering theological themes: our election in Christ before the foundation of the world, redemption through His blood, the mystery of the gospel uniting Jew and Gentile, and the calling to walk worthy of this high calling.

This week we explore Paul's opening praise for the spiritual blessings we have in Christ.

subsections.title: Greeting
subsections.content: Paul's opening greeting establishes his authority and the identity of his readers.

questions.question: Context: Who wrote this letter and by what authority? Who are 'the saints who are in Ephesus'? What do we know about the church there from Acts 19-20?
Observation: How does Paul describe himself? How does he describe the recipients? What two things does he wish for them?
Meaning: What does it mean to be 'faithful in Christ Jesus'? Why does Paul emphasize both 'grace' and 'peace'?
Application: Do you see yourself as a 'saint'—one set apart for God? How does your identity in Christ shape how you live?

subsections.title: Blessed in Christ
subsections.content: One of the richest passages in Scripture on the blessings of salvation.

questions.question: Context: This passage is one long sentence in Greek—a doxology of praise. What prompts Paul to write such an outpouring of worship?

Observation: List the spiritual blessings mentioned. Note the repeated phrase 'in Christ' or 'in him.' What role does each person of the Trinity play (Ephesians 1:3-6 Father, Ephesians 1:7-12 Son, Ephesians 1:13-14 Spirit)?

Meaning: What does it mean that God 'chose us in him before the foundation of the world' (Ephesians 1:4)? How does predestination relate to adoption (Ephesians 1:5)? What is the 'mystery of his will' (Ephesians 1:9)?
Application: How should the truth that God chose you before creation affect your sense of security and purpose? What does it mean to live 'to the praise of his glory' (Ephesians 1:12, 14)?

subsections.title: Paul's Prayer for the Ephesians
subsections.content: Paul prays for their spiritual enlightenment.

questions.question: Context: What has Paul heard about the Ephesians that prompts this prayer (Ephesians 1:15)?
Observation: What three things does Paul pray they would know (Ephesians 1:18-19)? How does he describe Christ's exaltation (Ephesians 1:20-23)?
Meaning: What is 'the hope to which he has called you'? What are 'the riches of his glorious inheritance in the saints'? How is Christ's power demonstrated in His resurrection and exaltation?
Application: Do you pray for spiritual knowledge and enlightenment for yourself and others? How does knowing Christ's supreme authority encourage you today?

subsections.title: Context for This Week
subsections.content: Paul now describes the radical transformation that has occurred in every believer—from spiritual death to spiritual life. This is one of the clearest passages on the doctrine of salvation by grace alone through faith alone. We were dead, but God made us alive. This is entirely His work, not ours.

subsections.title: Dead in Sin
subsections.content: Our condition before Christ—spiritually dead and under wrath.

questions.question: Context: How does this passage connect to Paul's prayer in chapter 1 about God's power toward believers?
Observation: What was our condition (Ephesians 2:1)? What three influences controlled us (Ephesians 2:2-3)? What were we 'by nature'?
Meaning: What does it mean to be 'dead in trespasses and sins'? If we were dead, what does this imply about our ability to save ourselves or even choose God on our own?
Application: How does understanding your former deadness increase your gratitude for salvation? How does 'children of wrath' describe all humanity apart from Christ?

subsections.title: Made Alive in Christ
subsections.content: The glorious 'But God' of the gospel.

questions.question: Context: What contrast does 'But God' introduce after the description of our deadness?
Observation: What motivated God to act (Ephesians 2:4)? What three things has God done for us (Ephesians 2:5-6)? What is His purpose (Ephesians 2:7)?

Meaning: How are we 'made alive together with Christ' when we were dead? What does it mean to be 'seated with him in the heavenly places'? How does God's saving us display 'the immeasurable riches of his grace'?
Application: How does the phrase 'But God' summarize your testimony? How does your salvation bring glory to God's grace for all eternity?

subsections.title: Saved by Grace Through Faith
subsections.content: The clearest statement of salvation by grace alone through faith alone.

questions.question: Context: How do these verses summarize what Paul has been teaching about salvation?
Observation: What is the source of salvation (Ephesians 2:8)? What is the means? What is excluded (Ephesians 2:9)? What is the result (Ephesians 2:10)?

Meaning: If salvation is 'the gift of God,' what does this exclude? How does verse 10 relate works to salvation—are they the cause or the result? What does it mean that we are God's 'workmanship' (poiema)?
Application: Are you resting in grace alone, or do you sometimes try to earn God's favor? What 'good works' has God prepared for you to walk in?

subsections.title: Context for This Week
subsections.content: Paul now addresses the unity of Jew and Gentile in Christ—a 'mystery' now revealed. The dividing wall of hostility has been broken down. Gentiles who were once far off have been brought near by Christ's blood. Together, Jews and Gentiles are being built into a holy temple—the dwelling place of God.

subsections.title: Once Far Off, Now Brought Near
subsections.content: The Gentiles' former exclusion and present inclusion.

questions.question: Context: Who is Paul addressing with 'you Gentiles'? Why does he remind them of their former condition?
Observation: List the five things that characterized Gentiles 'at that time' (Ephesians 2:12). What has changed (Ephesians 2:13)?
Meaning: What does it mean to be 'separated from Christ' and 'without God in the world'? How does 'the blood of Christ' bring those who were 'far off' near?
Application: Do you remember what life was like 'without hope and without God'? How does gratitude for being 'brought near' shape your worship?

subsections.title: Christ Our Peace
subsections.content: The wall of hostility broken down—one new humanity.

questions.question: Context: What 'wall of hostility' existed between Jews and Gentiles? How did the law create this division?
Observation: What has Christ done (Ephesians 2:14-16)? What did He preach (Ephesians 2:17)? What do both groups now have access to (Ephesians 2:18)?
Meaning: How did Christ abolish 'the law of commandments expressed in ordinances'? What is the 'one new man' He created? How does the cross reconcile us both to God and to each other?
Application: How should Christ's work of reconciliation affect how you view other believers from different backgrounds? Is there any 'wall of hostility' you need to let Christ tear down?

subsections.title: A Holy Temple
subsections.content: Built together into the dwelling place of God.

questions.question: Context: What imagery does Paul shift to in these verses? Why is 'temple' language significant for this audience?

Observation: What are Gentiles no longer (Ephesians 2:19)? What are they now? What is the foundation of this building (Ephesians 2:20)? Who is the cornerstone? What is the structure becoming (Ephesians 2:21-22)?
Meaning: How is the church the fulfillment of the Old Testament temple? What does it mean that Christ is the 'cornerstone'? How is the church growing into 'a holy temple in the Lord'?
Application: Do you see yourself as a living stone in God's temple? How does being 'a dwelling place for God by the Spirit' shape how you view the church?

subsections.title: Context for This Week
subsections.content: Paul explains his unique calling to preach 'the unsearchable riches of Christ' to the Gentiles. The mystery hidden for ages—that Gentiles are fellow heirs with Jews—has now been revealed. Paul then prays one of the most powerful prayers in Scripture: that they would be strengthened, rooted in love, and filled with all the fullness of God.

subsections.title: Paul's Ministry to the Gentiles
subsections.content: The mystery of Christ revealed to Paul.

questions.question: Context: Why does Paul call himself 'a prisoner for Christ Jesus on behalf of you Gentiles'? How does his imprisonment relate to his ministry?
Observation: What is the 'mystery' that was revealed to Paul (Ephesians 3:3-6)? How does Paul describe his calling (Ephesians 3:7-8)? What is God's purpose in revealing this mystery (Ephesians 3:10)?

Meaning: What does it mean that Gentiles are 'fellow heirs, members of the same body, and partakers of the promise'? How does the church display God's wisdom to 'the rulers and authorities in the heavenly places'?
Application: How does Paul's view of his calling as 'the very least of all the saints' challenge your own perspective? Do you see the church as displaying God's wisdom to spiritual beings?

subsections.title: Paul's Prayer for Strength and Love
subsections.content: A prayer for inner strength and the knowledge of Christ's love.

questions.question: Context: Why does Paul 'bow his knees before the Father'? What prompts this prayer?
Observation: What does Paul pray for (Ephesians 3:16-19)? List each request. What is the goal of this prayer?

Meaning: What does it mean to be 'strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being'? How can we 'comprehend' and 'know' the love of Christ that 'surpasses knowledge'? What does it mean to be 'filled with all the fullness of God'?
Application: How does this prayer shape your own prayers for yourself and others? What would it look like to experience 'the breadth and length and height and depth' of Christ's love?

subsections.title: Doxology
subsections.content: Glory to God who is able to do far more than we ask or think.

questions.question: Context: How does this doxology conclude Paul's prayer and the first half of Ephesians?
Observation: What is God able to do? According to what power? To whom is glory given and for how long?
Meaning: What does 'far more abundantly than all that we ask or think' reveal about God's generosity and power? Why is glory given 'in the church and in Christ Jesus'?
Application: In what area of your life do you need to trust that God is able to do 'far more than you ask or think'? How does this doxology lead you to worship?

subsections.title: Context for This Week
subsections.content: The second half of Ephesians begins with 'therefore'—because of all God has done (chapters 1-3), here is how you should live (chapters 4-6). Paul calls believers to walk worthy of their calling, maintain unity, use their gifts for building up the body, and put off the old self while putting on the new.

subsections.title: Unity in the Body of Christ
subsections.content: Walking worthy and maintaining the unity of the Spirit.

questions.question: Context: What is the 'therefore' referring back to? How does 'the calling to which you have been called' summarize chapters 1-3?
Observation: What character qualities does Paul list (Ephesians 4:2)? What are believers to maintain (Ephesians 4:3)? List the seven 'ones' (Ephesians 4:4-6).
Meaning: What does it mean to 'walk in a manner worthy of the calling'? How is unity maintained—is it created by us or given to us? What do the seven 'ones' reveal about the basis of Christian unity?
Application: Which of the qualities in verse 2 do you most need to grow in? Are you actively working to maintain unity in your church?

subsections.title: Gifts for Building Up the Body
subsections.content: Christ gives gifts to equip the saints for ministry.

questions.question: Context: How does this passage move from unity to diversity of gifts? What Old Testament passage does Paul quote (Ephesians 4:8)?
Observation: What gifts are listed (Ephesians 4:11)? What is their purpose (Ephesians 4:12)? What is the goal (Ephesians 4:13-15)? How does the body grow (Ephesians 4:16)?

Meaning: Why are apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds, and teachers given to the church? What does 'to equip the saints for the work of ministry' tell us about who does ministry? What does maturity look like (Ephesians 4:13-15)?
Application: Are you using your gifts to build up the body? Are you growing toward maturity, or are you still 'tossed to and fro' by various teachings?

subsections.title: The Old Self and the New Self
subsections.content: Put off the old, put on the new.

questions.question: Context: How does Paul describe the Gentile way of life that believers must no longer follow?
Observation: What characterizes the 'old self' (Ephesians 4:17-19, 22)? What must believers do (Ephesians 4:22-24)? What characterizes the 'new self'?
Meaning: What does it mean to 'put off your old self' and 'put on the new self'? Is this something that happens once or continually? How is the new self 'created after the likeness of God'?
Application: What aspects of the 'old self' do you still struggle to put off? What does 'being renewed in the spirit of your minds' look like practically?

gospelData.title: Week 6: Walk in Love, Light, and Wisdom

subsections.title: Context for This Week
subsections.content: Paul continues his practical exhortations: walk in love as Christ loved us, walk as children of light exposing the darkness, walk in wisdom making the best use of time. He addresses relationships in the household and concludes with the famous passage on the armor of God—our equipment for spiritual warfare.

subsections.title: Walk in Love
subsections.content: Imitating God as beloved children.

questions.question: Context: How do these verses connect to the forgiveness Paul just mentioned in 4:32?
Observation: What are believers called to be (Ephesians 5:1)? How are they to walk (Ephesians 5:2)? What is the model for this love?
Meaning: What does it mean to be 'imitators of God'? How is Christ's sacrifice described—'a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God'? How does this shape our understanding of love?
Application: How does Christ's self-giving love challenge the world's definition of love? What would it look like to 'give yourself up' for someone this week?

subsections.title: Walk as Children of Light
subsections.content: Exposing the darkness and living in the light.

questions.question: Context: Why does Paul transition from love to warnings about sexual immorality and impurity?
Observation: What things should 'not even be named among you' (Ephesians 5:3-4)? What warning does Paul give (Ephesians 5:5-6)? What does it mean to walk as 'children of light' (Ephesians 5:8-11)?
Meaning: What is 'the fruit of light' (Ephesians 5:9)? How do we 'discern what is pleasing to the Lord'? What does it mean to 'expose' the works of darkness rather than participate in them?
Application: Are there areas of darkness in your life that need to be exposed to Christ's light? How can you live distinctly as a 'child of light' in your context?

subsections.title: Walk in Wisdom
subsections.content: Making the best use of time and being filled with the Spirit.

questions.question: Context: How does walking 'carefully' and 'as wise' summarize the Christian life Paul has been describing?
Observation: What contrast does Paul make (Ephesians 5:15-17)? What does he command instead of drunkenness (Ephesians 5:18)? What are the results of being filled with the Spirit (Ephesians 5:19-21)?
Meaning: What does it mean to 'make the best use of the time, because the days are evil'? How is being 'filled with the Spirit' connected to singing, thanksgiving, and mutual submission?
Application: How are you using your time? What does it look like to be continually 'filled with the Spirit' in your daily life?

subsections.title: The Armor of God
subsections.content: Standing firm in spiritual warfare.

questions.question: Context: Why does Paul conclude with spiritual warfare? How does this connect to the 'rulers and authorities in the heavenly places' mentioned earlier?

Observation: What is the source of our strength (Ephesians 6:10)? Who is our real enemy (Ephesians 6:12)? List each piece of armor and its purpose (Ephesians 6:14-17). What accompanies the armor (Ephesians 6:18-20)?

Meaning: Why is our struggle 'not against flesh and blood'? What does each piece of armor represent—truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation, the word of God? Why is prayer essential to spiritual warfare?
Application: Which piece of the armor do you most need to 'put on' right now? How can you pray with 'all perseverance' for the saints and for the advance of the gospel?

subsections.title: Study Summary
subsections.content:
Key Themes of Ephesians:

  • Spiritual Blessings in Christ — Chosen, predestined, redeemed, sealed (1:3-14)
  • From Death to Life — By grace through faith, not works (2:1-10)
  • One New Humanity — Jew and Gentile reconciled in Christ (2:11-22)
  • The Mystery Revealed — Gentiles are fellow heirs (3:1-13)
  • Walk Worthy — Unity, gifts, putting off the old self (4:1-32)
  • Walk in Love, Light, and Wisdom — Imitating God, exposing darkness, being filled with the Spirit (5:1-21)
  • The Armor of God — Standing firm against spiritual forces (6:10-20)

Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with love incorruptible!
